Miroslavas Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Alytus County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Jews began settling in Miroslavas in the early 19th century; a synagogue was built in 1896, and the population reached 485 by 1897. During WWI, the retreating Russian army exiled Miroslavas's Jews to central Russia, and not all returned; the interwar period saw large-scale emigration to Palestine and the US. Only about 20 families remained by 1940; soon after the 1941 German invasion, all of Miroslavas's Jews were murdered in a nearby forest, alongside Jews from Alytus and other neighboring towns.
